a better understanding of the role played by the spatial resolution and scenario details in the prediction of pesticide fate and transport in surface water, and its relevance for the risk assessment of pesticides in the environment.

the development of the SoilPlus model to simulate the transport of pesticides from agricultural fields to surface waters, with the aim of improving predictions of the exposure of aquatic ecosystems to pesticides.

the improvement of the spatial and temporal representation of the SoilPlus model, which can be useful in the context of the European Union Water Framework Directive, where the use of models is required in order to evaluate the effects of diffuse sources of pollution on the quality status of surface water bodies.

the model can predict the fate of metolachlors and terbuthlyazine with an acceptable accuracy, and that a high resolution and a field-based approach are needed to improve predictions.

, although the model was not able to accurately predict pesticide concentrations in surface water at the basin scale, the model was capable of reproducing the observed patterns of pesticide concentrations, and that the use of high spatial resolution scenarios and field-based data improved model performance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a complex scenario, including a spatially-explicit approach, is necessary to obtain an acceptable prediction of pesticide runoff and river water concentrations.

a complex scenario is needed in order to obtain reliable estimates of the fate and transport of pesticides in the soil-river system, and that the SoilPlus model can be a useful tool to support risk assessment in small agricultural watersheds.

the SoilPlus-DynA model, with a high spatial resolution, a field-based database and a complex scenario, is able to predict pesticide concentrations in surface water, and thus to assess the exposure risk of aquatic ecosystem.

the model is able to provide reliable estimates of pesticide runoff and surface water concentrations, and can be used to assess the impact of agricultural practices on the environment.

a complex scenario, based on a spatially-explicit model and a field-based database, can provide a better representation of pesticide fate in runoff than a simple scenario based on a non-spatially-explicit model.
